newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude market dominated by WAf sales.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude market dominated by WAf sales.

text.p: Asian crudes remained steady in quiet trading, with refiners more focused on buying western crudes priced against Brent and WTI, traders said.
A Chinese company confirmed buying July loading North Sea Oseberg and Argentinian Escalante crudes from two western traders, probably for processing at the Guangzhou refinery.
The details of the trades were not confirmed, but heard to be for 1.8 million barrels of Escalante at WTI -$2.90 per barrel c+f, and a similar volume of Oseberg.
A 1.2 million barrel cargo of Egytian Gulf of Suez was also heard sold to south Korea.
West African cargoes continue to flow into Asia, with a 900,000 barrel cargo of Bonny Light heard sold to a Japanese refiner. The refiner is heard looking for more barrels.
A South Korean refiner was also heard buying its first cargo of Bonny Light from a European major.
Spot prices of Yemeni crudes remain supported by the relatively low Brent levels, with a 600,000 barrel August Masila cargo heard done to a South Korean refiner at OSP +20/25 cents per barrel.
This is the second August deal for Masila, traders said.
But trading for other Middle East crudes was thin.
Widespread rumours that a western trader sold its Dubai cargo to a US major on Wednesday was denied by the trader.
Another western trader holding an Oman cargo said there was no necessity for it to sell its barrels, leaving just two partial Oman cargoes on offer for July.
Buyers of Asian light crudes were also sidelined in a bearish market, with Belida heard offered marginally lower at ICP +30/40.
An Indonesian affiliate with 300,000 barrels of July Belida was heard having difficulties finding buyers.
